original_question: Let M ⊂ P n be a compact odd dimensional CR manifold. Find conditions on M which ensure that M bounds a complex variety.(This is well understood in C^n .) -N.Sibony, sibony@anh.matups.fr
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the short open problem in The Several Complex Variables Problem List attributed to N. Sibony: determine what conditions on a compact odd-dimensional CR submanifold of projective space ensure that it is the boundary of a complex variety, in contrast with the affine case in C^n, which the draft itself notes is already well understood.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient projective setting (P^n), the object M as a compact odd-dimensional CR manifold, and the central boundary question: when M bounds a complex variety. It also preserves the paper's intent that the projective-space version is the unknown one, unlike the affine C^n case.
missing_details: P^n should be specified as complex projective space CP^n.
Because M is written as a subset of P^n, the question should explicitly say that M is embedded in CP^n.
The real dimension of M should be written as 2p-1, so the expected complex dimension of any filling variety is p.
The smoothness/regularity of M is implicit in the phrase CR manifold and should be made explicit if the question is to stand alone.
The notion of 'bounds' should be clarified: existence of a pure p-dimensional complex analytic variety (or holomorphic chain) V in CP^n \ M whose boundary is M.
It should be stated whether singularities of V are allowed in the interior; the phrase 'complex variety' normally allows this, but a stand-alone question should say so explicitly.
The boundary should be interpreted in the geometric/current sense, not merely topologically.
Orientation of M is implicit in any boundary formulation and should be made explicit if one wants a completely stand-alone research question.

The draft does not say whether the desired conditions are meant to be necessary and sufficient, or only sufficient; the paper's wording is informal, but a sharpened research question should ask for a characterization.
The phrase 'This is well understood in C^n' is contextual rather than part of the mathematical statement and should be converted into scope-setting language rather than left as a parenthetical aside.
refined_question: Let M \subset \mathbf{CP}^n be a compact embedded smooth CR manifold of odd real dimension 2p-1. What necessary and sufficient conditions on M ensure that there exists a pure p-dimensional complex analytic variety V \subset \mathbf{CP}^n \setminus M, allowed to have interior singularities, such that M is the boundary of V?
justification: The paper is not a theorem/proposition article but a problem list, and the accessible arXiv record explicitly says it contains a Scratchpad section for vaguely formulated conversational questions. Your draft already matches that style and clearly targets the Sibony projective-space boundary problem rather than a broader neighboring topic. Since no sharper formal theorem statement is supplied nearby in the accessible paper metadata, the most faithful refinement is to keep the exact projective-space boundary problem, while only unpacking the implicit mathematical data needed to make it stand alone: CP^n as the ambient complex projective space, the odd real dimension 2p-1 of the CR manifold, the corresponding expected complex dimension p of the filling, and the meaning of 'bounds a complex variety' as existence of a pure-dimensional complex analytic filling with possible interior singularities. The paper's own abstract also confirms that such entries may be intentionally informal, which explains why the original draft omits these details.
